messages:
Maya R.: FYI noticed a big capacity drop in us-west-2 this morning after the gpu-operator helm upgrade. Pods are stuck in Init with driver errors.
Jon H.: Ugh, what version did we move to?
Maya R.: gpu-operator v1.14.0 -> changed device-plugin restart behavior, and a couple kernel modules failed to load.
Priya S.: Can you paste the kubelet / device-plugin logs?
Maya R.: Sure — here's a snippet from node gpu-node-23: 
```
Jun 10 08:12:01 gpu-node-23 kubelet[2345]: E0610 08:12:01.123456 2345 device_plugin.go:215] device plugin handshake failed: incompatible driver version: kernel module reports 525.85, nvidia-smi returns 470.182
Jun 10 08:12:02 gpu-node-23 kernel: nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol nvidia_pci_register_driver
Jun 10 08:12:03 gpu-node-23 device-plugin[5678]: failed to allocate devices: no healthy GPUs
```
Jon H.: That symbol mismatch screams kernel/driver mismatch. Did nodes get a host-driver update?
Maya R.: Not intentionally. Looks like the operator pushed the containerized driver installer that picked a newer driver build for some node pools (we have mixed kernel versions across the fleet).
SRE Lead: Current impact: capacity down ~38% in us-west-2 (autoscaler scaled up but pods pending), a few job queues backed up.
Priya S.: Workaround: cordon affected nodes, drain non-critical jobs, and roll back the operator?
Maya R.: I tried: 
```
helm rollback gpu-operator 1 -n gpu-operator || helm upgrade --install gpu-operator redwood/gpu-operator --version 1.13.2 -n gpu-operator
kubectl cordon gpu-node-23
kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```
Maya R.: Rolling back the operator prevented new installs, but the nodes that already applied the newer driver still show dmesg errors.
Jon H.: Can we force reinstall the kernel modules matching the older driver? Risky across many kernel versions.
Priya S.: Two mitigation paths: 1) Re-image affected nodes to a known baseline kernel+driver (slow, safe). 2) Taint them and move traffic to other pools temporarily (faster but costs more).
SRE Lead: Ops decision: prioritize stability. Start taint+drain for customer-facing pools and spin a temporary dedicated pool in another AZ. Keep finance in the loop — this will increase hourly GPU spend.
Maya R.: Also seeing NCCL WARNs in some pods: `NCCL WARN Call to cuDeviceGet failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN` — likely cascading from driver mismatch.
Jon H.: Good call. Also grep kubelet logs for device-plugin handshake errors across the cluster: `journalctl -u kubelet | grep device-plugin | grep handshake` — getting a list now.
engops-bot: Incident ticket #INC-2026-594 created for us-west-2 GPU regression. Pager sent to oncall.
Priya S.: I'll run a query to list nodes with mismatched module version: `for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o name); do ssh $n "modinfo nvidia | grep -i version"; done` — will post results.
Maya R.: We should also pin the operator's driver-install image to the tested build and add a preflight kernel check in the upgrade pipeline. Learned the hard way. :grimacing:
SRE Lead: Agreed. After recovery: add a canary rollout policy for operator updates (1% of nodes). Also add alerting for device-plugin handshake failures and kernel-driver symbol mismatches.
Jon H.: I'll prepare the rollback PR and the temporary taint script. Priya — ping me the node list when you have it.
Priya S.: Posted node list and versions in the ticket. Short term plan documented there.
Maya R.: Thanks all — will monitor capacity and post updates in the ticket. :eyes:
